A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CARSO and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Shared content can be matched despite retitling, scenario renumbering and substantial revisions to the evaluation.

before.justification: V1 reports original clean and adversarial classification experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D, plus training-development observations and an internal-representation perturbation experiment.

after.justification: V3 reports original classification experiments, training times and a large-perturbation robustness test in Section 5, alongside preliminary experimental observations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The reported encoder architecture omits Dropout(p=0.0375), present in v1 Table 3 but absent from v3 Table 4. The conditional VAE, representation conditioning, balanced-batch training and shared classifier remain. Sum-of-softmax aggregation was already used for v1's end-to-end evaluation.

E1.justification: CIFAR-100 is added for training and evaluation alongside retained CIFAR-10. MNIST and Fashion-MNIST lose their full quantitative benchmark evaluations, but remain as datasets used in qualitative preliminary experiments in v3 Appendix C; their use is therefore not entirely removed.

E2.justification: V3 evaluates Cui et al. (2023) pretrained Wide ResNet baselines and adds numerical state-of-the-art reference comparisons, including Chen et al. (2023) purification with reported CIFAR-10 robust accuracy of 73.24%. The Wong and Rebuffi comparators are retained despite renumbering and corrected architecture naming.

E3.justification: V3 centers CARSO evaluation on end-to-end rand-AA and drops the separately reported classifier-targeted attack evaluations. The added Wide ResNet scenarios use eight reconstructions and distinct training budgets, including 200 epochs, batch size 128 and adversarial fraction 0.12 for CIFAR-100. The shared models retain four reconstructions and the existing 20-EOT, 100-step adaptive evaluation.

E4.justification: V3 adds an epsilon=0.9 test across all four scenarios to investigate gradient obfuscation. It removes v1's detailed attack-type/strength sweeps and the direct internal-representation perturbation experiment reporting 0.0406 accuracy. The qualitative investigation motivating balanced batches is retained in Appendix C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. Reconstruction counts and EOT iterations describe inference and attack procedures, rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V3 Table 2 adds Wide ResNet CARSO robust accuracies of 0.7570 on CIFAR-10 and 0.6573 on CIFAR-100, alongside new clean, baseline and stress-test results. Shared Wong/Rebuffi end-to-end accuracies remain exactly 0.7096 and 0.6648. V1's classifier-targeted CARSO accuracy column and detailed supplementary benchmark scores are removed.

T1.justification: The PGD objective and update equations move from Section 3 to Appendix A, while the unchanged VAE derivation moves from Appendix A to B. No new theorem, proof or substantive formal assumption is introduced; revisions to the gradient rationale remain conceptual.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes improving adversarially trained classifiers, including its selected state-of-the-art ResNet-18 setting. V3's abstract and conclusion claim overall CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 robustness leadership over adversarial training and purification approaches. It also presents the conditional VAE as one implementation of a broader purifier-independent framework.

C2.justification: The gradient-interference rationale and principal clean-accuracy/scalability limitations persist. V3 newly attributes the clean-accuracy penalty specifically to the VAE and suggests diffusion or score-based replacements. It also explicitly limits the preliminary MNIST/Fashion-MNIST experiments to training-protocol development, rather than evidence of end-to-end robustness.

D1.justification: V3 supplies Wide ResNet layer subsets, scenario-specific hyperparameters, training times and one/eight-GPU allocations. New Appendix E explains layer-selection heuristics that v1 left largely unspecified. Conversely, v1's explicit normalization statistics and small-classifier architecture details are omitted. The CARSO code-access disclosure is retained.

R1.justification: V3 replaces the robust-overfitting/weight-averaging discussion with synthetic-data training, modified losses and robustness-oriented architectures, adding works including Cui, Peng and TRADES. Chen's diffusion classifier and gradient-obfuscation literature also enter the positioning. Comparisons now explicitly target leading purification as well as training approaches, while the original integration-novelty claim remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and contribution narrative are rewritten, with extensive revisions to architectural explanations, experimental discussion and limitations. Formal PGD material moves into the appendices, which are reorganized around retained theory, preliminary experiments, implementation details and new layer-selection guidance.

P2.justification: The architecture schematic is retained, reduced and moved from v1 Appendix E/Figure 5 to v3 Section 4/Figure 1. The main accuracy table is substantially redesigned, runtime and gradient-obfuscation tables are added, and all four accuracy-change plots are removed. Appendix tables are restructured around the revised scenarios.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the empirical relevance through stronger pretrained baselines and CIFAR-100, clarifies which experiments evaluate end-to-end robustness, and adds a gradient-obfuscation sanity check and practical layer-selection guidance. These improve support and reproducibility beyond v1. The net gain is limited by removal of detailed attack-strength sweeps and the representation-perturbation diagnostic; the shared models' adaptive evaluation and results were already present in v1.
